newsitem.title: SPAIN: Clinton, Blair hold unscheduled meeting.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Blair hold unscheduled meeting.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and British Prime Minister Tony Blair held an unannounced meeting on NATO issues and the Northern Ireland peace process late on Monday night, the White House said on Tuesday.
The two leaders met for about 90 minutes at Clinton's Madrid hotel after a NATO summit dinner at Moncloa Palace hosted by Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar.
It was another example of the growing close personal relationship between Clinton and Blair, who share a political philosophy and style of leadership.

"At the conclusion of dinner, he (Clinton) invited Prime Minister Blair to come back and (they) presumably had a refreshment or two. Mrs Clinton was there as well," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

McCurry said the two men discussed topics related to the summit and other bilateral issues, including the U.S.-supported Anglo-Irish push to end more than 25 years of sectarian strife in Northern Ireland.

A small group of reporters that tracks the president's movements was not informed of the meeting at the time it occurred. McCurry confirmed that Clinton and Blair had met in response to questions from the media.
